u6581cc8cb5: Programming a device chip uses the VBAT, DM, DP and GND pins. Solder communication wires to these pins (in mass production, the device provides programming points for these pins, which are contacted by the probes of a fixture) and connect them to the corresponding pins of a USB male connector, then plug it into a USB female programming port of the 1-to-8 programmer to program the device chip firmware. This is shown in ⟦1⟧Device chip programming wiring⟦/1⟧ and ⟦2⟧Contact points reserved on the device for mass-production programming⟦/2⟧.

u730dcde957: When you need to program bare chips with the 1-to-8 programmer, you can use a demo board with a socket for the corresponding chip, or the top board of the 1-to-2 programmer for that chip. The wiring for programming through a top board is shown in ⟦1⟧Top board programming wiring⟦/1⟧.

u2fe6877f01: The programmer firmware is the firmware of the main controller chip that controls the operation of the whole programmer. ⟦1/⟧Before programming the target chip firmware, be sure to check whether the current programmer firmware version is the latest; ⟦2/⟧if it is not, update to the latest ⟦3/⟧programmer firmware version through a remote upgrade (except in special cases), ⟦4/⟧otherwise some programming problems may occur.
u2d58475b10: The target chip firmware means the fw, ufw and key files; ⟦1/⟧these files must be updated to the programmer and stored there so that the corresponding data can be programmed into ⟦2/⟧the target chip during programming, or used for verification and blank check; ⟦3/⟧when updating the target chip firmware, you also need to set the programming options ⟦4/⟧to enable functions such as resource programming and chip performance tests
u8add7db4c8: Working modes include programming, verification, blank check, current test, etc.; ⟦1/⟧be sure to confirm the programmer's current working mode to avoid programming problems
u490b6a772f: Program the device chip firmware manually or automatically
u09d8fcefb8: Manual programming means programming by plugging and unplugging devices by hand, or by pressing a fixture onto the devices ⟦1/⟧to make contact; automatic programming means that the programming of the device chips is controlled by an automatic programming handler
u4c076a8a0f: ⟦1⟧Offline programming⟦/1⟧: programming that does not require a PC. With the 1-to-8 programmer, the target chip firmware is first deployed from a PC to the programmer's memory and stored there; the chips are then programmed offline.

u13c0950daa: Before programming, verifying or blank-checking chips, you need to update the programmer with the programming firmware for the target chip, that is, the fw or ufw file built by the SDK, or the key file. During programming, the programmer programs this firmware into the target chip, or uses it for verification and blank check. If the programmer has already been updated with the corresponding firmware, skip the steps in the following subsections.

ua88972c56b: [3] Right-click the "CD Drive" and open it; you will see the ⟦1⟧burner.exe⟦/1⟧ file, the user manual and other files;

u0f7abc3dc8: Before programming the device chip firmware, make sure you have carried out the related operations in ⟦1⟧the first 4 subsections⟦/1⟧ to avoid problems during programming. These operations include:
uf731e22197: Power on the programmer before programming and wait for the ready-to-program screen (see the "⟦1⟧Power on the programmer⟦/1⟧" subsection)
u70dc6912e1: Confirm that the target chip firmware currently in the programmer is the firmware to be programmed, or update it (see the "⟦1⟧Update the target chip firmware on the programmer⟦/1⟧" subsection)
ue185960b4d: Prepare the devices to be programmed, with their USB interface brought out, or the mass-production devices and the dedicated fixture.
uaa903d8743: When the preparations for programming are complete, power-cycle the programmer and turn on the USB power toggle switch so that the programmer display is in the ready-to-program state.
uc6fb2c9beb: When the programmer detects that a USB male connector wired to the VBAT, DM, DP and GND pins of a device chip has been plugged into a USB programming port, it starts programming the firmware of the device chip on that channel.
u9bfe3679f7: There are therefore two ways to program devices:
u6af00d7849: First turn on the USB power toggle switch, then plug the USB male connector wired to the VBAT, DM, DP and GND pins of the device chip into the female programming port of the programmer. Use this method to program a single device, or for press-contact programming with a fixture in mass production.
ud3d8772b93: First plug the USB male connector wired to the VBAT, DM, DP and GND pins of the device chip into the female programming port of the programmer, then turn on the USB power toggle switch. Use this method when you need to program several devices at the same time outside mass production and without a fixture.
u4b1b906c61: Starting programming with method 1 is illustrated in ⟦1⟧Steps to start programming a single device⟦/1⟧ and ⟦2⟧Steps to start programming with a fixture⟦/2⟧.

u3fcd5cfb97: A programming fixture can be extended to press down on and contact the USB test points (VBAT, DM, DP, GND) of Nx8 devices at the same time, so that N programmers can program Nx8 device chips simultaneously.
